summary: Verified the intro-tour.mp4 trim (first 7s removed). Asset is served correctly and is a valid H.264/AAC MP4. Regression on /safety-assessment, /problem-solving, /prep/child-goals, /: no console errors. NOTE: Actual visual playback of the trimmed video inside IntroTourModal could NOT be visually confirmed in Playwright because Playwright's headless Chromium ships without proprietary H.264 codec support (canPlayType('avc1.*') returned ''). We confirmed this is a Playwright limitation — the untouched /intro-tour.original.mp4 fails with the exact same 'DEMUXER_ERROR_NO_SUPPORTED_STREAMS' inside Playwright — so it is NOT a regression caused by the trim. Real user browsers (Chrome/Edge/Safari/Firefox) will decode this file normally.

modal_integration.note: Because Playwright Chromium can't decode H.264, video.error was code 4 for BOTH the trimmed and original files. Real Chrome/Edge/Safari support this codec by default.

regression_checks./: loads, no console errors, hero CTA opens IntroTourModal with correct trimmed video src

action_items: None required for the trim itself — asset is valid H.264/AAC MP4, faststart, 70.067s, byte-identical between local and CDN. Visual playback should be verified once in a real Chrome/Edge browser by a human, since Playwright's headless Chromium lacks H.264 support.

OPTIONAL: If you ever want automated Playwright visual verification of this video in the future, consider providing an additional WebM/VP9 <source> in IntroTourModal.jsx, since Chromium OSS supports WebM natively. Not required for real users.
critical_code_review_comments: IntroTourModal.jsx: the video has a single <source> via src attribute (H.264 only). This is fine for real browsers but breaks in Playwright Chromium and would also break in any pure Chromium build without proprietary codecs. Adding a WebM fallback would make it more robust and testable.

IntroTourModal uses ?v=branded-2026-06-17 as a cache-buster in the src — after this asset change, the query string wasn't updated. Since Cache-Control is 'no-store, no-cache, must-revalidate' from the server it isn't blocking, but bumping the query string (e.g., ?v=branded-2026-06-17-trim7s) would be a cleaner practice to guarantee stale CDN/browser caches are invalidated for returning users.

success_rate.frontend: 100% for what could be tested — HTTP delivery, content-length, duration, ftyp/moov, faststart, byte-identical CDN payload, modal DOM integration, Skip button, and regression across /safety-assessment, /problem-solving, /prep/child-goals, /. Actual video decoding in the browser was unverifiable in Playwright due to Chromium OSS H.264 limitation (same behavior on untouched original file), NOT a regression.

seed_data_creation: In-browser: seeded localStorage['sac_legal_ack_v1'] with {version:'v1', at:...} and localStorage['sacoparents.orientation_seen.v1']='true' to bypass modals. Also cleared 'sac_intro_tour_seen_v3_branded' to force IntroTourModal to appear.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Playwright's bundled Chromium (HeadlessChrome/145.0.7632.0 on this env) DOES NOT support H.264 — video.canPlayType('video/mp4; codecs="avc1.*"') returns ''. This means <video> elements pointing to any H.264 MP4 will emit MEDIA_ERR_SRC_NOT_SUPPORTED (code 4) with 'DEMUXER_ERROR_NO_SUPPORTED_STREAMS'. Do NOT interpret this as a broken asset — verify by testing a known-good MP4 (e.g., /intro-tour.original.mp4). To confirm an MP4 is well-formed inside this env, use ffprobe on the file and curl -I on the URL (200 + video/mp4 + expected Content-Length). WebM playback works ('probably'). If future automated tests need to visually verify intro-tour playback, add a WebM source to IntroTourModal or use a headed browser with proprietary codec support.
rca_of_the_issue: N/A — trim change is working correctly. The only observable 'issue' (video error in Playwright) is a testing-environment limitation, not a product bug. Root cause: Playwright's Chromium build omits proprietary H.264/AAC codecs; the same error occurs on the pre-trim original file, ruling out any encoding regression from the ffmpeg re-encode.
